glosses: jemanden zur Erfüllung einer Aufgabe bestimmen; jemanden als Bevollmächtigten an einen Ort oder in ein Gremium delegieren

examples.text: „Da nach demselben die Stadtverordneten-Versammlung das Recht hat, in das Gymnasial-Curatorium einen Bürger hiesiger Stadt zu deputieren, so wählte dieselbe den Buchdruckerei-Besitzer Herrn Griebsch zum städtischen Mitgliede.“ (1871)

translations.source_sense_description: jemanden zur Erfüllung einer Aufgabe bestimmen; jemanden als Bevollmächtigten delegieren

glosses: To officially empower, authorize, pronounce, and establish (someone) to be a deputy.
to officially empower and authorize (someone) to act as a substitute in one's role or office

examples.text: I deputize you to act for me while I'm away.

glosses: To act as a substitute for a person in their role or office

examples.text: Gringoire, on the other hand, stuck with equal firmness to the fact that he was deputizing for a brother officer who was sick — so sick that he had mislaid his orders.

What he wanted was someone who could really deputize for him when he was away on business – clearly not the job for a secretary but, because of years of experience and a willingness to take responsibility, one that the previous holder of the post had taken on.
It is commonly used in the theatre where an understudy essentially deputizes for an indisposed actor.
